title: Track / logic ground truth (OR, visible_none, bounded counts, occlusion, fragmentation)
description: Ground truth for the bounded-logic and track-derived predicates. Encodes the safety rules from §2.2, §14.3, §22.1(9-10): visible_none requires an assessable observation interval with complete expected observation ticks; counts are over qualifying anonymous tracklets in ONE continuous camera interval and must become `unresolved` under unsafe fragmentation/occlusion. Missing coverage can never become a clean negative.

alternatives.description: Small, explicit list of visible alternatives (bounded OR). No open-world reading.

present_alternatives.description: Which alternatives are actually visibly present in the assessable scope.

target.description: The object/attribute whose visible absence is asserted inside the interval.

assessable.description: Whether the target region is assessable throughout the interval.

expected_observation_ticks.description: Number of sampling ticks that MUST be present to certify absence.

observed_ticks_complete.description: Whether all expected observation ticks are actually present. If false, absence cannot be certified.

expected_outcome.description: visible_absence_supported requires assessable=true AND observed_ticks_complete=true. Otherwise unobservable (region unjudgeable) or unresolved (missing coverage) — never a clean negative (§14.3). Enforced by eval/schema.py cross-field check.

qualifying_tracklets.description: Ground-truth count of qualifying anonymous tracklets in ONE continuous camera interval. Never crosses cameras or discontinuous intervals.

declared_bound.description: Configured maximum bound. Counts exceeding the bound route to clarification/unsupported (§3.3).

fragmentation_level.description: Track fragmentation severity. `high` forces `unresolved` regardless of raw count.

expected_outcome.description: Either an integer count (only safe when fragmentation/occlusion are not severe and the count is within the declared bound) or the literal `unresolved`. Enforced by eval/schema.py cross-field check.
